doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Wrong notes, trumpet embouchure and staying healthy
summary: There are no wrong notes unless uncorrectable; trumpet lacks saxophone's cover, depends on embouchure, and he keeps healthy without a routine.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: And is there anything that constitutes a mistake or a wrong note for you?
Only if you can’t correct it. So that comes with years of experience you know. Doorbell — You’re going to have to cut this
Well I’ve had that discussion about wrong notes with a number of people and they agree with you, you’re going to play them you just have to deal with it.

Well there are no wrong notes. What I mean by that is not intentionally — saxophones, you know because of the pads and they have to use all of their fingers. They have a lot more possibilities for covering what they might consider a mistake. But you know for brass, the trumpet, you have no such support you know. You have these three valves and you have three fingers to work with. Everything you do has to be controlled by your diaphragm and your embouchure. And your embouchure will, I mean sometimes the setup is just, it won’t respond right. And it also depends on your dental setup and you

know you have to know how the trumpet — when there’s a danger that it’s not that you don’t know what you want to do and where you want to go with something you know, it’s how well the embouchure is set up to deliver it.
Do you have a regimen that you do to try to stay healthy and as capable of playing what’s in your head and physically making it happen?
Yes. To not abuse myself in any form so that my physical self will be able to deliver, then it’s about how well I utilize that with the instrument. I don’t have a routine you know.
